diagrams.title: Vulnerabilities ↔ Impact Matrix
diagrams.subtitle: Each cell shows the most likely impact. Click a cell to understand the exploitation path.

cells.detail: A patch exists or existed: the attacker uses a public exploit against an exposed service.
An arbitrary read flaw allows retrieving data stored on the host.
An unpatched kernel or system service grants administrator privileges.
A memory management flaw causes the process to terminate.
The attacker installs persistent access on an unmonitored host.
The window between check and use is exploited; a macro or hardcoded secret triggers execution.
An unhandled exception reveals data or credentials.
Input validation is insufficient or bypassed by malicious input.
Unbounded input exhausts application CPU or memory.
A trusted update channel drops a persistent component.
Stale or unrotated credentials allow running commands under a legitimate identity.
A permission misconfiguration grants access to out-of-scope data.
An unapproved service or identity provider issues valid tokens to the attacker.
A rogue device or modified setting makes the service unavailable.
An ownerless account remains a permanent access path.
A hypervisor flaw allows code execution on the host.
A rogue access point or compromised device captures traffic.
An open port or overly permissive firewall rule crosses the zone.
An unfiltered exposed service is overwhelmed by traffic.
An unpatched guest serves as a persistent foothold.
An external document or instruction pushes the model to execute an action.
Publicly accessible secrets or objects are retrieved without authentication.
Tokens or excessive roles grant access to multiple applications.
A compromised or unavailable third party blocks the service.
A component added to the model or storage maintains access.
